Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency & Redwood rate limits

Hi CJ / Adam -

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery on concurrency and perf SLOs so we have a shared next step list: 

Summary of Nimbus requirements (as I heard them):
- User-facing chat: target median latency 100-200ms (streaming responses)
- Peak concurrent active chat sessions: ~300 (spiky distribution during business hours)
- Background jobs / async inference: up to 4,000 parallel short-lived requests at peak (lower latency requirement but high concurrency)
- Peak throughput: ~10k requests/min across endpoints
- Streaming required for user-facing flows (progressive tokens + partial-rendering)

Ask for us: please confirm the numbers above and add any missing use-cases. I attached the spreadsheet we discussed to capture per-endpoint concurrency and sequence length distribution (nimbus_concurrency_requirements.xlsx).

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
1) Can you confirm the per-endpoint concurrency numbers in the sheet by EOD Friday?
2) We’ll propose an initial hosted quota and fallbacks; if you need guaranteed headroom we’ll scope Dedicated/reserved capacity options and pricing.
3) Internal tech check - I’ll loop in our infra lead (Dylan) to confirm pooling/connection patterns and whether we should recommend a per-client connection pool or a proxy layer.

Initial note on rate limits (short version): our hosted defaults are conservative - account-level token and request rate limits plus per-route concurrency caps. For pilots we usually provide a temporary quota bump so you can run load tests; if you need sustained throughput we recommend a reserved capacity (Dedicated) commitment which gives predictable throughput and higher concurrency SLOs. I’ll attach a short quota proposal in the next email.

Thanks - Marissa

Thanks Marissa - this looks right, appreciate the recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 300 concurrent chats is correct for our interactive web app. Those are long-lived streaming connections (typically 30-90s).
- The 4k background jobs are short (200-800ms) but they come in bursts - they’re from our realtime enrichment pipeline.
- For the interactive flows we’d like to avoid head-of-line blocking: ability to support 250-300 parallel streaming streams with per-session low latency.
- We’ll likely have a third channel (mobile app) that multiplexes connections but can add another ~100 concurrent streams at peak.

Questions: 
1) What are the exact hosted API rate limit numbers we should expect (requests/sec and concurrent request caps) and how do those translate to token-based billing?
2) For connection pooling: should we be pooling sockets to Redwood endpoints or using a proxy that multiplexes HTTP/2 streams? Any SDK guidance?
3) What does a pilot look like (duration, cost, and can you provide a temporary quota increase so we can run an end-to-end load test)?

I’ve attached a short internal note so you can see the burst pattern. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

-CJ
CJ Harper
Head of Infrastructure
Nimbus AI

Thanks CJ - great questions. High-level answers below; I’ve attached an initial quota proposal (redwood_initial_quota_proposal.pdf) with concrete numbers and a recommended pilot plan.

1) Hosted API rate limits (typical):
   - Default account-level sustained rate: 60 requests/sec (burst to 120 for short windows)
   - Default per-route concurrency cap: 50 simultaneous requests
   - Token billing is per-token; rate limits are orthogonal but we can provide headroom for pilots

   For your profile (streaming + many short jobs) we typically propose a temporary pilot quota of:
   - Account-level rate: 200 req/sec sustained (burst 400)
   - Per-route concurrency caps: 200 for user-facing chat route; 400 for background-job route
   - Total account concurrency cap: 600

2) Connection pooling / SDK guidance:
   - Recommended: use HTTP/2 with multiplexed streams where possible and maintain a small number of long-lived connections per host.
   - For very high short-lived bursts (your background jobs) we recommend a short-lived connection pool + exponential backoff on 429s; batching on the client side when possible.
   - Our SDKs support streaming and automatic reconnects; we also provide a lightweight proxy pattern for customers who want to do aggressive multiplexing and connection reuse.

3) Pilot:
   - Duration: 2 weeks of controlled load (we provide quota bump and monitoring hooks).
   - Cost: pilot under hosted with temporary quota increase; standard pay-as-you-go token billing applies. If you need a sustained uplift beyond pilot we can scope Dedicated reserved capacity with a month-to-month or annual commit.

Next steps:
- If those pilot numbers look reasonable I’ll request a temporary quota bump from infra and schedule a 30-min runbook review with Dylan and your infra team.
- Please confirm the per-endpoint concurrency in the attached spreadsheet so we can finalize the pilot config.

Marissa

Thanks Marissa - quick confirmation from infra:

- Pilot numbers are feasible. We can provision a temporary quota bump: account-level 200 req/sec sustained, burst 400, per-route caps as proposed (200 for chat, 400 for background). We’ll monitor token consumption and latencies during the test window.
- Recommendation for Nimbus: use HTTP/2 multiplexing with 4-8 long-lived connections per pod and enable per-client connection pooling at the proxy layer. That pattern reduces TCP churn and preserves KV cache locality for streaming sessions.
- Caveats: streaming sessions keep KV cache warm; very high churn of unique model contexts can increase memory pressure - we should advise a short warmup period and pre-warming of common prompts where possible.
- Rollout plan: we’ll grant the pilot quota for 14 days; infra will enable tracing hooks and a temporary dashboard so Nimbus can watch p99/p50 latency and request/429s. If they need sustained capacity beyond pilot we should move to a Dedicated quote.

I’ll create the quota ticket and the temporary dashboard today. Marissa - please confirm pilot start window and I’ll assign the infra tasks.

-Dylan
